messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

**Subject: [Service Name] moves to [New Platform] on [Date]**

Hi [Name],

Next quarter [Service Name] moves to [New Platform]. Your account, your data, and your billing history all come with it. You won't re-enter anything or chase a second round of approvals.

Why now: we've run [Service Name] on [old stack] since [year], and there's no room left to build on it. [New Platform] makes space for [specific capability, e.g. per-project permissions and an audit log], which customers have asked for repeatedly.

**What changes**

- From [date], sign in at [new URL]. The old address forwards for 12 months.
- Send API traffic to [new endpoint]. Existing keys keep working, and the current endpoint stays live until [sunset date].
- [Feature X] works differently now. See [link].

**What stays the same**

Pricing, contract terms, support hours, and your data retention settings.

**The cutover**

We move accounts in batches starting [date]. Yours is in [window]. Expect a reminder a week ahead, and another that morning. Access drops to read-only for about [N] minutes while we switch you over. Reply to this email if that timing doesn't work and we'll put you in another batch.

If anything looks off afterward, write to [support address] with MIGRATION in the subject. That queue is separate, and staffed through [date].

[link] covers the rest: API changes, the full timeline, and the rollback plan.

— [Name], [Title]

---

Fill in the brackets. Two of them set your ticket volume: why you're moving now, and the [Feature X] line. Vague answers there create the support load.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
